_note: Topic backlog. These are editorial seeds, not facts: the research agent must still find and read sources before anything is written. Order is by priority within each category; the planner rotates categories so the site never looks one-note.

topics.title: How to Compare AI Tool Pricing Without Getting Burned
topics.notes: Focus on seat-based vs usage-based billing, annual lock-in, overage rules, and the second-year price. Use official pricing pages only.

topics.title: AI Tool Free Tiers: What the Limits Actually Mean
topics.notes: Translate vague 'limited' claims into concrete caps where the vendor documents them. Where they do not, say so plainly.

topics.title: When an AI Tool Is Not Worth the Subscription
topics.notes: Decision rules for cancelling: usage below a threshold, work that needs auditability, tasks where the free tier suffices.

topics.title: Reading an AI Vendor's Data Policy in Ten Minutes
topics.notes: Retention, training opt-out, subprocessors, deletion on cancel. Quote the policy text; do not paraphrase legal terms loosely.

topics.title: Build a Research Workflow with an AI Assistant
topics.notes: Source collection, extraction, contradiction logging, and a final verification pass. Include a worked example with a neutral topic.

topics.title: Writing Prompts That Survive a Model Upgrade
topics.notes: Why brittle prompts break, what to pin (constraints, format, examples), and how to test a prompt against two models.

topics.title: Turn a Messy Document into a Structured Brief
topics.notes: A repeatable extraction pattern: entities, decisions, open questions, owners. Warn about hallucinated detail.

topics.title: A Repeatable Way to Fact-Check AI Output
topics.notes: Claim extraction, primary-source matching, time-sensitivity checks, and how to record what could not be verified.

topics.title: Web App or Desktop App: The Real Trade-offs
topics.notes: Offline access, data locality, update cadence, integrations, and the failure modes of each. No product endorsements.

topics.title: What to Check Before Trusting a New SaaS Tool
topics.notes: Export options, uptime history, security page, company age, pricing change history. Cite what the vendor publishes.

topics.title: Exporting Your Data Before You Cancel a Subscription
topics.notes: What export formats actually preserve (structure vs text), and what is usually lost. Practical, checkable steps.

topics.title: Designing an Automation That Fails Safely
topics.notes: Idempotency, retries with backoff, dead-letter handling, alerting, and a kill switch. Include a failure checklist.

topics.title: Which Tasks Should Never Be Automated
topics.notes: Low-frequency, high-consequence, judgement-heavy, or relationship-critical work. Give a decision test, not opinions.

topics.title: Connecting Two Tools Without Writing Code
topics.notes: Trigger/action mapping, field matching, rate limits, and when the no-code path becomes a maintenance trap.

topics.title: How to Read an AI Model Release Note
topics.notes: Separate what shipped from what was announced, check the date and the model name, and find the limits section. Use a real, current release note as the worked example.

topics.title: Separating an AI Benchmark from an AI Claim
topics.notes: What a benchmark measures, who ran it, on what data, and why a headline number rarely transfers to your task.

topics.title: Chatbot vs Search Engine for Research
topics.notes: Where a chatbot saves time, where it invents, and the hybrid workflow that beats both. Test criteria stated up front.

topics.title: Local AI Models vs Cloud AI Models
topics.notes: Cost at volume, privacy, latency, capability gap, and hardware requirements. Be explicit that the gap moves monthly.
